transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-23
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (Parkview Head of Security), Priya Desai (Platform Engineer), Karen Liu (PM)

Summary (auto-generated, may be rough): quick POC weekly check-in focused on security/compliance items: SSO setup (SAML + SCIM), audit log retention and forwarding, data residency/retention policy, KMS/HSM support, SOC 2 evidence sharing, and next steps for tests and docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll run for about 45 minutes, main focus security items for the POC — SSO, logs, retention, and SOC2 artifacts. michelle sorry, michael?
[00:10] Michael: no, all good, thanks Alex. quick note — timeline is still end of Q1 for production decision but security sign-off needs to be in Jan.
[00:18] Alex: perfect. Samira, do you want to kick off with SSO/SCIM?
[00:22] Samira: sure. so we deployed the test tenant last week and Parkview user reprovisioning worked, there were a couple of mapping issues — displayName mapping came in as display_name in your IdP, small mismatch. i pushed a workaround but we'll include a note in the SSO doc.
[00:36] Priya: yep we saw that. we also want SCIM to auto-provision and deprovision groups for role-based access. what's Redwood's current SCIM support level?
[00:44] Samira: we support SCIM 2.0, group sync is supported but there are some attribute name diffs depending on IdP. we provide a sample mapping and a small adapter in the repo. for the POC we can patch mapping on our side if you prefer, long term we'd recommend aligning IdP attributes.
[00:58] Karen: any MFA constraints for SSO sessions? our policy enforces adaptive MFA for admin roles.
[01:04] Samira: Redwood respects the IdP session — so MFA is IdP-driven. admin actions in the console are RBAC-controlled; you can require SSO+MFA via your provider. we can document the admin role list.
[01:16] Michael: ok good. next, audit logs — we need full audit trails for all model invocations and console actions, with at least 90 days retention and the ability to export to our SIEM (Splunk).
[01:26] Alex: current default retention is 90 days in hosted by default; we also offer log-forwarding to customer-managed S3 or direct Splunk/Honeycomb endpoints — Samira you can confirm.
[01:33] Samira: yeah, we can stream structured audit logs (JSON) to your Splunk HTTP Event Collector or to an s3 bucket. note: payloads that contain raw user content are redacted unless you opt-in; we keep operation metadata (request id, model, token counts, user id, timestamp). if you need full content logs for debugging we can enable with customer-controlled access and encryption.
[01:53] Priya: encryption — at rest and in transit? we require kms-backed encryption for logs and keys stored in our HSM.
[01:59] Alex: Redwood supports AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit. for customer-managed keys we integrate with cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) and have HSM options for private deployments. we'll include KMS integration notes in the doc pack.
[02:14] Michael: SOC2 — can you provide the Type II report and any compensating controls we should be aware of?
[02:19] Alex: yes, we'll send the most recent SOC2 Type II along with our security controls summary and the pen-test executive summary. note that some details are in the secure share link.
[02:27] Karen: curious about data residency — our regs require customer data to remain in our region for EU customers. can Redwood pin data to region?
[02:34] Samira: for Private deployment yes. for hosted we offer regional tenancy — we can pin your tenant to eu-west-1 region so data storage and processing remain in EU. we'll provide the diagram showing data flow and where logs are stored.
[02:47] Priya: what's the behavior for cache / KV cache? do we persist any request data outside ephemeral GPU memory?
[02:54] Samira: we maintain a KV cache in memory for request performance, it's ephemeral and not written to disk. any persistent caching (prefix cache) is optional and encrypted; we can disable persistent caching for your tenant during POC if preferred.
[03:08] Michael: good. also need to confirm user access reviews and admin RBAC — our audit requires quarterly access review evidence. how does Redwood expose admins / tokens list?
[03:17] Alex: we expose admin audit logs and a user list export from the console, with role assignments. we can give you a CSV export and an API endpoint to pull current roles.
[03:26] Samira: there was a small hiccup in the demo where service tokens weren't labeled clearly; Samira note — we will ensure token naming and last-used timestamp show up in the next build.
[03:36] Priya: for log forwarding, can you send a sample payload so we can confirm Splunk parsing?
[03:41] Samira: yes — will send a sample JSON log (with redacted PII) and a Splunk HEC example config.
[03:48] Karen: any compliance gaps re: PCI/HIPAA? we have some teams that handle PHI, others that are just PCI scoped.
[03:56] Alex: Redwood has customers in regulated spaces; for PHI we recommend Private or Dedicated with strict network controls and BAA discussion. we do not sign BAAs on hosted by default — that's a contractual discussion. PCI usually works with encryption, tokenization, and limited PII in logs. we'll note recommended deployment for PHI workflows.
[04:14] Michael: can we run a tenant-level penetration test? we prefer to run our standard tests against the tenant.
[04:20] Alex: yes, we support customer-run pen tests; we just need a schedule and scoping doc. our security team will coordinate the pre-authorization.
[04:28] Samira: also want to call out rate limits and throttling — for production we can set custom quotas for your tenant; during the POC we saw one edge case where long-sequence generation hit a soft-limit, we tuned batch size and it's better now.
[04:42] Priya: perfect. last thing — single-tenant PIIs: do you store any user-provided content in persistent logs?
[04:48] Samira: by default content is ephemeral; persistent logs redact content. we can enable full-content logging to a customer-managed S3 bucket encrypted with your KMS if you want to keep full records, with access controls.
[05:01] Karen: okay, recap and next steps?
[05:04] Alex: recap — Alex to send SOC2, pen-test summary, network diagram; Samira to send SAML/SCIM metadata, sample audit logs, and Splunk config; Priya to validate log forwarding; customer to propose pen test dates and confirm compliance scope. we will sync next week at the same time.
[05:20] Michael: thanks everyone.
[05:22] Alex: thanks, speak soon.

References / Shared artifacts mentioned:
- SOC2 Type II report (to be shared via secure link)
